newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suspected Carlos accomplice extradited to France.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Carlos accomplice extradited to France.

text.p: Margot Froelich, a German suspected accomplice of guerrilla Carlos the Jackal, will be extradited to France from Italy on Thursday for questioning on bombings carried out in France in 1982, justice sources said.

The sources said Italian authorities had agreed to extradite Froelich, who was arrested in Rome in October 1995. Carlos, whose real name is Ilich Ramirez Sanchez, has been held in a French jail since August 1994.

The sources said that Froelich would arrive in France later on Thursday and would be questioned by anti-terrorism investigating magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere, who is leading probes into several attacks blamed on Carlos.

French authorities suspect Froelich drove a car from former Yugoslavia which, after being packed with explosives, blew up in Paris on April 22, 1982, killing a pregnant woman and wounding 63 other people.

The target of the attack was the weekly Arab newspaper, Al Watan Al Arabi, known for its critical stance towards left-wing Arab governments. But it is also thought to have been aimed at forcing the release from French jail of two other Carlos accomplices.
Files from the former east German secret services also link Froelich to the bombing of the Paris-Toulouse express train in France in March 1982, which killed five people.
